topics.justification: Centered on "attack", "implementation", "protocol", "standard", and references to proofs/papers and primitives (hash/signature), suggesting discussion of how real-world implementations and protocol choices deviate from standards and create exploitable weaknesses.

topics.topic_name: Symmetric encryption basics: keys, randomness, OTP
topics.justification: Dominated by "key", "message", "encryption/encrypt/decrypt", "plaintext/ciphertext", "random", and "time_pad", indicating questions about correct key generation/length, randomness, and fundamental secure encryption patterns (including one-time pad).

Top terms like "password", "hash", "attacker", "crack", "store", "server", and "compromise" strongly point to secure credential storage, threat models involving database leaks, and choosing schemes that resist brute-force/offline attacks.

topics.topic_name: Designing crypto algorithms (and why they get broken)
topics.justification: Words such as "algorithm", "break", "design", "cipher", "cryptographer", and "year" reflect meta-level discussions about creating new cryptography, the difficulty of doing so, and the common reasons homegrown designs are eventually broken.
